failure_summary.description: Choices either omitted a theorem-supported refinement or added an unsupported one, often by guessing rather than verifying the precise difference between similar options.

patch.reasoning: The errors go in both directions, so a general instruction to choose stronger or safer claims would not help. A focused comparison of the exact differences between close options can prevent both missed refinements and unsupported additions.

edits.content: - When choices share a base claim but differ by a refinement, isolate that exact difference—such as a domain restriction, uniformity of constants, parameter dependence, or an added conclusion—and verify it directly against the applicable result. Do not choose the base claim merely because the refinement is unfamiliar, or accept the refinement because it sounds plausible. If choices are not nested, assess their differing clauses independently rather than assuming a single strength ranking.
